note: AI-driven third-party security risk management (San Francisco). BCV's listing: 2021, Early (Rak Garg, Enrique Salem); Bain Capital Ventures was an existing investor when the company raised $7M in November 2024, $24M in total (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/viso-trust-secures-24m-to-accelerate-innovation-in-ai-powered-third-party-risk-management-302312499.html). Protecht acquired it in April 2026 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260420190963/en/Protecht-Acquires-Leading-AI-powered-Risk-Platform-VISO-TRUST). The 2021 round is not named, and the Early tag never mints a stage (decisions.md R2).

Virtual lab management for development and test (Santa Clara, per the firm's archived listing). 'VMLogix Receives Funding from Bain Capital Ventures' (InfoWorld, 2006-10): a $3.5M Series A from BCV (Ajay Agarwal). 'VMLogix was acquired by Citrix Systems in August 2010' (the firm's archived page).

E-business applications and internet frameworks (San Jose). The firm listed it from its 2003 page, 'Early', and as acquired by 2006; no source read names the acquirer. BCV held it by 2003; the round is not named.

Marketplace and tools for digital creators (Brooklyn, New York). 'In June 2024, Whop raised US$50 million in a Series B round led by Bain Capital Ventures at a valuation of US$800 million' (Wikipedia); a Series B entry reads Growth, matching the listing's Growth tag (Merritt Hummer). Mark: Tether's $200M investment at $1.6B (February 2026), aligned with Insight.

Point-of-sale consumer financing for service businesses (San Francisco). Greylock led the 2019 seed and Series A; 'Existing backers Greylock Partners and Bain Capital Ventures also participated' in the $45M Series B Insight led (TechCrunch, 2021-09-09, https://techcrunch.com/2021/09/09/wisetack-closes-on-45m-to-bring-buy-now-pay-later-to-in-person-services/), so BCV entered before September 2021 in a round no source names (the firm's 2022 archive: Matt Harris). Momentum check (fintech): no priced round at $1B or more since the 2021 Series B; the 2025 Group 1001 deal is a lending capital partnership. Aligned with Greylock and Insight.

Marc Lore's food delivery and fast-casual food hall company (New York). BCV's listing: 2020, Early (Scott Friend); the 2020 round is not named. Mark: the $650M round of July 2026 at a $9B pre-money valuation (Restaurant Dive, 2026-07-16). Sibling Accel (same company, Sameer Gandhi) reads below_1b with no mark; this cited round is fresher evidence. The EQT Ventures (wonder.me, Berlin) and First Round (research service) rows named Wonder are different companies.

Work apparel and footwear retail chain (Weymouth, MA in the firm's 2006-2013 listings, 'Expansion/Growth Buyout'). Its CEO bought it out of bankruptcy in 2002 and raised about $40M from venture investors (Wikipedia, Anthony DiPaolo); no source read gives BCV's round or stake, so the listing bucket stays context. It filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025, moved to liquidate and closed its stores in February 2026 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/n-gear-closes-west-springfield-224938798.html); a family office-backed operator bought its assets in April 2026 (https://www.pr.com/press-release/965089): an asset sale out of a wind-down reads acquired (COLLECTION.md s6).

Self-serve business intelligence for commerce brands (New York). BCV led the $4.4M seed (AlleyWatch, announced 2022-12-20; the firm's listing: 2021, Seed, Scott Friend), after a $1M pre-seed Primary led in 2021 without BCV. M13 led the $9M Series A with BCV participating (Pulse 2.0, 2024-10-01).

Crypto and stablecoin settlement infrastructure (Chicago), formerly the Seed CX exchange (the 2022 archive renders Zero Hash at /portfolio/seed-cx; the seed-cx row folds in here). BCV led Seed CX's $15M Series B in September 2018 (CryptoSlate; the firm's 2018 listing, Salil Deshpande); a Series B entry reads Growth. Renamed Zero Hash with a Series C in 2020; 'Bain Capital' joined the $105M Series D of January 2022. Mark: the $104M Series D-2 Interactive Brokers led in September 2025 at $1B (CoinDesk). Mastercard's reported $2B takeover talks ended without a deal in January 2026 (https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/01/26/zerohash-is-in-talks-to-raise-usd250-million-at-usd1-5-billion-valuation-after-walking-away-from-mastercard-takeover), so private.
